note: The thin shared reference the two agents construct for the DC underlay/overlay seam. Identity-only entries for the seam concepts, plus the native-only concepts named apart so the 'zone' trap binds correctly. No entry for opaque vendor tags. Crucially, avail-zone and sec-zone are DISTINCT entries, so two concepts both labelled 'zone' bind apart rather than merging.

entries.label: underlay binding
entries.definition: The point where an overlay segment is bound onto the underlay on a leaf/VTEP for local delivery.
entries.example: the binding of tenant-blue on leaf-3

entries.label: tenant segment
entries.definition: One tenant broadcast domain at the seam, carried as a local VLAN in the fabric and identified as a VNI in the overlay.

entries.label: fabric edge device
entries.definition: The leaf switch (and its co-located VTEP) where servers and overlay bindings meet the fabric.

entries.label: fabric MTU
entries.definition: The MTU carried across the fabric, sized so encapsulated overlay frames are not fragmented.

entries.label: tenant default gateway
entries.definition: The L3 default gateway for a tenant segment, realised as an SVI in the fabric or a distributed anycast gateway in the overlay.

entries.label: spine switch
entries.definition: A spine switch forming the fabric backbone; a fabric-internal concept with no overlay counterpart.

entries.label: availability zone
entries.definition: A physical fault domain of the fabric (power/cooling/pod boundary); a fabric-internal 'zone', unrelated to a policy grouping.

entries.label: micro-segmentation policy
entries.definition: A policy controlling which workloads may communicate within and across overlay segments; an overlay-internal concept with no fabric counterpart.

entries.label: security zone
entries.definition: A named grouping of workloads to which micro-segmentation rules attach; an overlay-internal 'zone', unrelated to a physical fault domain.
